//: This file is a complete config as it is: copy it to config.json and run. No other target
works without filling its config in.
The tests start their own app server and DB server, in docker containers, and run against them.
Nothing of yours is changed: the .env of the checkout is only read, and a server you have
running on the checkout (and its DB) is left alone — both can run at the same time.
What is started, and kept for the next run unless docker.keepRunning is false:
memo-e2e-db   MariaDB with its data in memory (fast, and gone when the container stops).
memo-e2e-php  The app, from the image of the app's own container, serving this checkout
with an .env of its own: a copy of the checkout's .env with the DB replaced
Needed on this machine: docker, the image of the app's container (`docker compose build`
in the checkout), and the mariadb client programs (mariadb, mariadb-dump).
The frontend: the app loads it from the Vite dev server. If one is running on the checkout
(your own dev container), it is used. If none is, one is started in memo-e2e-php, on
docker.vitePort; the two can run side by side, and the app uses the one started last.
The tests log in as a global admin they create in the new DB (also with docker.base "copy");
a run logs its e-mail and password at the start, for you to log in to that server too.
To start over with a new DB: `docker rm -f memo-e2e-db`. Changing docker.base does the same.

ui.// baseURL: Where the app container serves the app. Pick a free port; not the one of your own server.

// base: "empty"  The app's migrations and nothing else. Needs no access to any other DB. The
"copy"   A copy of the DB that the checkout's .env points at, taken when the container is
made. Shows that the tests also pass next to real data, as they have to on an rc
server. The credentials are read from that .env and used for the one dump only.
// optional: The rest can be left out; these are the defaults.
memoDir      The checkout to serve; relative to the playwright directory.
appImage     The image for the app container.
dbPort       The port of this machine the DB container is reached on (by the tests only).
vitePort     The port for a Vite dev server started by the tests; not the one of your own.
keepRunning  Leave the containers running after a run, so the next one starts at once.
